forms.plain_english: The catch-all current report: a company must tell the market within four business days about defined material events, each filed under a numbered Item (1.01 material agreements, 1.02 terminations, 1.05 cyber incidents, 2.02 earnings, 2.03 debt, 5.02 officer/director changes, 5.03 bylaw changes, 5.07 vote results, 7.01 Reg FD, 8.01 other, 9.01 exhibits). Item 2.02 and 7.01 content is 'furnished', not 'filed'.
forms.who_files_when: All six companies. Deadline: 4 business days after the triggering event (Item 5.07: 4 business days after the meeting; Item 2.02: on the earnings release; Items 7.01/8.01 voluntary, no deadline). Observed latency in the filings read: Apple 5.02 event 2026-04-17 (Fri) filed 2026-04-20 (Mon); Netflix 5.02 event 2026-04-10 filed 2026-04-16 (exactly the 4th business day); Berkshire 5.02/5.07 event 2026-05-02 (Sat) filed 2026-05-07 (4th business day); Microsoft 5.02 event 2026-06-02 filed 2026-06-05; Amazon 1.01 event 2026-06-08 filed 2026-06-10; Amazon 5.07 meeting 2026-05-20 filed 2026-05-22; Amazon 5.02 event 2026-09-08 filed 2026-09-09. Frequency in the latest 10 filings (Atom feed): Apple 10 in ~15 months, Microsoft 10 in ~12 months, Alphabet 10 in ~6 months (heavy: ATM and capital raise), Netflix 10 in ~9 months, Berkshire 10 in ~10 months, Amazon 10 in ~6.5 months. Roughly 10-20 per year each.

companies.frequency: ~10/yr (latest plain 8-K: 2026-07-30 acc 0000320193-26-000018, Items 2.02, 9.01). Latest entry on feed is an 8-K/A (Item 5.02).

notes: ITEM 5.02 EXTRACTION FIELD LIST (ticket 20): filing: accession, form (8-K vs 8-K/A), filed_at, event_date (dei:DocumentPeriodEndDate), parent_accession for amendments, deadline_met flag (business days between event and filing <=4), sub-item code (a=departure/resignation/termination, b=departure of named executive officer or director, c=appointment of principal officer, d=election of director, e=compensatory arrangement, f=NEO compensation not available at proxy time). person: full name, age, title before, title after, role type (CEO, CFO, PAO, director, chair, lead independent director, executive chair), board committees, independent flag, prior employers and tenure, tenure at company. event: change type (appointment, resignation, retirement, termination, will-not-stand-for-reelection, role change), effective date, announcement date, trigger text, reason (disagreement yes/no and quote), successor name and interim flag, predecessor name, whether successor named, next shareholder meeting reference. compensation: base salary, cash bonus, sign-on, equity award grant value or share count, vehicle type (RSU/PSU/GSU/options), vesting schedule, performance metric (e.g. relative TSR vs S&P 500), severance, retirement perqs (e.g. Berkshire NetJets 30 hours, ~$490,000/yr, through 2037-05-31), tax gross-up flag, plan name, agreement exhibit number (EX-10.x). governance: indemnification agreement flag, family relationships, related-person transactions (e.g. Amazon Mandia: sister-in-law employee $185,000 salary, 103 RSUs), amendment-promised flag (Apple: intends to file amendment under Item 5.02(c)(3)). confidence and source-span offsets.
Three-plus worked 5.02 examples are in executives findings: Apple CEO succession and 8-K/A, Berkshire CFO succession, Microsoft Hoffman, Netflix Hastings, Amazon Mandia, Alphabet Saraci.
Four-business-day rule reference: Item 5.07 deadline runs from the meeting date; 8-K/A for 5.02(c)(3) runs from the date compensation is determined.

Summary of top two ideas: (1) Officer-change feed with comp extraction and 8-K/A chaining; (2) Shareholder-vote results dataset with per-proposal counts. Third: successor/predecessor CIK lineage from 8-K12B; fourth: debt/material agreement event feed.
Follow-up done: 8-K12B exact-match checked for all six (only Alphabet filed one). 8-K/A history pulled. Apple R1.htm confirmed dei fields. Findings tagged source_method.
